---
title: "Presets and protocols"
---

## Presets

A preset is a reusable setup for one canonical capability. It can fix configuration values, declare runtime inputs and provide a fast launch path from the dashboard or a widget.

A good preset avoids accidental capture of one-off operator text. If a value is fixed by the preset, the user should not be forced to enter it again during the run.

## Protocols

A protocol composes multiple capability/preset steps. The protocol does not own alternative versions of those capabilities; it invokes the same canonical method contracts.

The runner must preserve explicit step state and give the operator rails: where they are, what just happened, what is next, and whether retry/cancel/continue is appropriate.

## Results

Individual step results are available to the protocol runner, and the final protocol result may combine useful outputs. Closeout semantics should be as clean as single-capability runs: no unnecessary generic result detours and no loss of launch-origin context.
